task.text:
Kenji,

Exploring the terminal with this much care has clarified the real issue for me, so thank you.

This also feels like an exciting point at which to expand the evaluation. Rather than continuing to judge the capital V by itself, I would like to see how its gesture carries into both the lowercase v and the É accent. Because the right arm will ultimately define all three forms, viewing them together should tell us whether we have truly established the architectural language of the complete Veillvé identity.

My preference remains Option 2 from the prior round, but I no longer think my eye is reacting to the terminal itself. The concern seems to be the final section of the right arm that leads into it. Could that last stretch hold just a little more confidence before finishing, allowing the gesture to continue with conviction instead of softening as it nears the end?
